about.title: Fort Jones Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Fort Jones is a town of about 695 people, and a loss here is felt on every block of Main Street. In 2025, public records show the city logged zero injury collisions and zero traffic deaths, which is worth acknowledging. Still, wrongful death claims in Siskiyou County do not come only from crashes. They can follow a fall at a rental property, a mistake in medical care, an incident on a ranch or job site, or a collision out along SR-3 where the town gives way to open valley. California law lets certain family members bring a civil action when a death results from another party's negligence or wrongful act. A spouse or domestic partner and children have the first right to file; other dependents or heirs may qualify in some situations. Recoverable losses include funeral and burial expenses, the financial support the person would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. We handle wrongful death cases on contingency, so you pay nothing unless we recover on your behalf.

whyChoose.title: Why Fort Jones Families Choose Us

items.title: Standing questions get answered early
items.desc: California limits who may file a wrongful death claim, starting with a spouse or domestic partner and children, then certain dependents and heirs. We can tell you quickly whether you qualify.

items.title: Deadlines are tracked from the start
items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of death to file, and far less time when a public agency such as Caltrans or the county is involved. Getting in touch sooner protects that window.

items.title: No fee unless there is a recovery
items.desc: We take wrongful death cases on contingency, so a grieving family in Siskiyou County does not have to pay up front.

items.question: My relative was killed in a crash on Highway 3 outside Fort Jones. Does a state highway change anything?
items.answer: It can. If part of your claim involves a road condition, sign, or maintenance issue on SR-3 or another public road, a government entity may be a party, and California requires a formal claim against that agency on a much shorter timeline than the usual two years. That is why it helps to speak with us promptly rather than waiting for the crash report to be finalized.

items.question: Who is allowed to bring a wrongful death case in California?
items.answer: The surviving spouse or registered domestic partner and the children have the first right to file. If there is no one in that group, other heirs or people who were financially dependent on the person, such as a parent or stepchild in some circumstances, may have standing. We can sort out who should be part of the case so nothing is left out.

items.question: There is already a criminal case. Do we still need a civil claim?
items.answer: Yes, they are separate. A criminal prosecution is brought by the state and focuses on punishment, while a wrongful death suit is a civil action brought by the family to recover funeral costs, lost financial support, and the loss of companionship and guidance. Your claim can proceed regardless of how the criminal matter turns out.
